name: 49ers
subhead: 2026 training camp edition — a veteran core coming off 50-plus missed starts, two new veteran receivers, and one question: is there enough left?

left.title: Front Office & Leadership
items: The premise of the offseason: health. San Francisco's starters missed a combined north of 50 games in 2025, systematically dismantling Shanahan's timing-based scheme before the season reached January.
The season ended 41–6 in the divisional round at Seattle — a result that framed every decision that followed.
The strategy: rather than rebuild, San Francisco bought proven veteran production at receiver and interior defensive line, betting the existing core plays.

QuestionNational previews put it directly: did the Niners do enough this offseason? Signing a 32-year-old receiver coming off an eight-game season is a departure from the youth-and-speed identity the front office had been building.

left.title: Trades & Major Transactions
items: SignedMike Evans, WR — three years, $60.4M, ending his 12-year run in Tampa Bay. Six-time Pro Bowler and Hall-of-Fame-track producer, but 32 and coming off an injury-plagued eight-game season.
TradeOsa Odighizuwa, DT acquired from Dallas for San Francisco's 2026 third-round pick — completed two days after the Evans signing.
SignedWR Christian Kirk — the intermediate-route complement to Evans, in a room that otherwise lacked proven options.
SignedOL Vederian Lowe (2 yr) and OL Brett Toth (1 yr) — depth for a line that has to protect better inside.
Re-signedTE Jake Tonges on a two-year deal.

right.title: Player Updates & Camp Battles
items: Brock Purdy, QB. Reported fine after the shoulder trouble that shaped his 2025. The whole offense's ceiling still runs through him.
Fred Warner, LB. Already cleared — the most encouraging health item on the board.
Nick Bosa, EDGE. Potentially back at the start of camp.
George Kittle, TE. Optimistic about a Week 1 return.
Left guard is the camp battle that matters. Interior pressure disrupted the 2025 offense more consistently than edge pressure did — and it lands directly on Purdy.
Mike Evans & Christian Kirk. Both must be synchronized with Purdy almost immediately; Shanahan's offense does not reward newcomers who need half a season.
Youth gets reps. With Kittle, Bosa and Warner all managing toward September rather than August, young players will see heavy camp volume — and some will win jobs.

right.title: The Bottom Line
items: San Francisco's 2025 was not a talent problem, it was an availability catastrophe — and the response was to add two veteran receivers and an interior rusher rather than reshape the roster. That works only if Bosa, Kittle, Warner and Purdy are all standing in January. The optimistic read is a Hall-of-Fame core with reinforcements. The pessimistic read is that the same core is a year older, a 32-year-old receiver is the marquee addition, and Seattle just put 41 on them. Left guard, of all things, may decide which one it is.
